name: bitwuzla
desc: SMT solver for bit-vectors, floating-points, arrays and uninterpreted functions
why: An SMT solver for bit-vectors and floating point, a fascinating logic engine though fairly specialist.

brief.what_it_is: Bitwuzla is an SMT (Satisfiability Modulo Theories) solver. It takes logical formulas over fixed-size bit-vectors, floating-point arithmetic, arrays and uninterpreted functions, and their combinations, and decides whether they are satisfiable. The sources say it is distributed as a command-line program named bitwuzla, and it also has C, C++, Python and OCaml APIs. The sources do not describe the exact input format or the output in detail.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives the framing as a solver for the theories of fixed-size bit-vectors, floating-point arithmetic, arrays, uninterpreted functions and their combinations. The name comes from an Austrian dialect expression meaning 'someone who tinkers with bits'.
brief.how_it_works: The README and homepage do not explain the internal mechanism. The CAV 2024 news item on the homepage mentions a paper titled 'Scalable Bit-Blasting with Abstractions', which suggests bit-blasting is part of the approach, but I did not read that paper and cannot confirm it from the pages.
brief.install_notes: The README says Bitwuzla builds on Linux and macOS, and on Windows via MSYS2 or cross-compiled with Mingw-w64. Detailed build instructions are in docs/install.rst in the repository, which I did not fetch. The docs index lists 'Installation and Build Instructions', 'Building Bitwuzla on Linux and macOS', 'Python Bindings', 'Building Bitwuzla for Windows' and 'Command Line Interface' pages, none of which I opened. I did not see any runtime, account or hardware requirement.
brief.standout: The project's own write-up is careful about its niche: it is a solver for bit-precise and floating-point reasoning, the kind used in verification and symbolic execution, not a general-purpose tool. Its name comes with a pronunciation guide, and the homepage credits a CAV 2023 Distinguished Paper Award and a string of SMT-COMP division wins.
brief.status: The homepage's news list runs through SMT-COMP 2023 and a CAV 2024 paper, and the repository has a CI badge on the main branch, so the project looks active. I did not see a release date or last commit date, so I cannot give a precise status. Best guess: maintained, but this is inferred from the news list and CI badge rather than a dated release.
brief.caveats: The project is specialist: useful mainly to people working in SMT, formal verification or symbolic execution. Build instructions live in docs/install.rst, which I did not read, so build difficulty is unknown. The README says Windows support goes through MSYS2 or cross-compilation with Mingw-w64, not a native build. The brew description and the scout notes both call it a specialist tool. The brew caveats field is empty.
quotes: Bitwuzla is a Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) solver for the theories of fixed-size bit-vectors, floating-point arithmetic, arrays, uninterpreted functions and their combinations.
Its name is derived from an Austrian dialect expression that can be translated as 'someone who tinkers with bits'.
Bitwuzla can be built on Linux, macOS. For Windows, it can be built using MSYS2 or cross-compiled via Mingw-w64.
